intro: Today you learn **will**, a small word with big jobs. You use it to say what you think will happen (I think it will rain), to offer help and make promises (I'll help you), and to decide something right now (There's no milk? I'll buy some). Warm-up: how do you say 'Saya janji' in English?
teachingNotes: Form: will + base form (the verb as in the dictionary) for every subject: I will go, she will go (never 'she will goes'). No 'to' and no -ing after will: stress the common errors *'I will to call you tonight' (→ I'll call you tonight) and *'I think it will raining' (→ I think it will rain). am/is/are become 'be' after will: It will be hot, not *'It will is hot'. Short forms: I'll, you'll, he'll, she'll, it'll, we'll, they'll; will not → won't. 'won't' is irregular (not 'willn't') and is said like 'don't' with a w ('wount'), not like 'want'.

Indonesian trap 1: 'akan' covers both will and going to, so learners can't tell them apart from Indonesian. Indonesian trap 2: Indonesian often uses no future word at all for offers and quick decisions ('Saya angkat', 'Nanti saya telepon', 'Saya ambil yang putih'), so learners say *'The phone's ringing. I answer it.' / *'I call you later.' / *'I take the white one.' Whenever the learner offers, promises or decides on the spot, check for 'll.

Uses taught here: (1) predictions as opinion with I think / maybe / I'm sure / I don't think (I don't think Budi will come is more natural than I think Budi won't come, but both are correct); (2) offers (I'll help you, I'll pay) and promises (I'll call you tonight, I won't forget, I promise I'll…); (3) decisions made at the moment of speaking (I'll answer it, I'll have the soto ayam, please, I'll take the white one).

Will vs going to (the learner knows going to from the previous lesson): going to = a plan from before you speak (you already have the tickets, the paint) or a prediction from what you can see now (Look at the clouds!); will = you decide now, or it's just your opinion. For opinion predictions both are often fine (I think it will rain / I think it's going to rain): accept both there and only mark will wrong when there is a clear plan from before, and going to wrong when the decision is clearly made right now.
Placement: 'maybe' at the start (Maybe she'll be late). Questions with will (Will it be hot tomorrow?) can be shown but are not tested.

Limits: the learner has NOT learnt the past simple (only was/were) or the present perfect, so don't use 'I bought / I've bought' in examples; give clues in the present (I have the tickets). Don't teach 'shall' (Shall I…?), first conditionals (If it rains, I'll…), the future continuous or 'would' beyond the A1 phrase 'would like'.

keyPoints.title: Predictions: I think … will + verb
keyPoints.explanation: To say what you think will happen, use will + the base form of the verb, the same for every subject. Start with I think, Maybe, I'm sure or I don't think. After will, am/is/are become be (It will be hot). No 'to' and no -ing after will.

examples.en: I think it will rain this afternoon.
examples.id: Saya rasa nanti sore akan hujan.

examples.en: Maybe the bus will be late.

examples.id: Saya yakin kamu akan suka Bandung.

id.title: Prediksi: I think … will + kata kerja
id.explanation: Untuk mengatakan apa yang menurutmu akan terjadi, pakai will + bentuk dasar kata kerja, sama untuk semua subjek. Awali dengan I think, Maybe, I'm sure atau I don't think. Setelah will, am/is/are berubah menjadi be (It will be hot). Tidak ada 'to' dan tidak ada -ing setelah will.

keyPoints.title: Offers and promises: I'll … / I won't …
keyPoints.explanation: When you see a problem, offer help with I'll + verb. To give your word, promise with I'll or I won't (= I will not). Indonesian often has no future word here (Nanti saya telepon), but English needs will: I'll call you later, not 'I call you later'.

id.title: Menawarkan bantuan dan berjanji: I'll … / I won't …
id.explanation: Saat kamu melihat ada masalah, tawarkan bantuan dengan I'll + kata kerja. Untuk berjanji, pakai I'll atau I won't (= I will not). Bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakai kata 'akan' di sini (Nanti saya telepon), tapi bahasa Inggris butuh will: I'll call you later, bukan 'I call you later'.

keyPoints.title: Deciding now: will · plans from before: going to
keyPoints.explanation: Use will when you decide at the moment you speak: something happens and you choose what to do. If the plan is from before (you already have the tickets), use going to. Indonesian 'akan' covers both, so look at the situation, not the Indonesian word.

examples.en: The phone's ringing. I'll answer it.
There's no sugar. — OK, I'll buy some.
I have the tickets. We're going to watch the film on Saturday.
examples.id: Saya sudah punya tiketnya. Kami akan nonton film itu hari Sabtu.

id.title: Memutuskan sekarang: will · rencana dari sebelumnya: going to
id.explanation: Pakai will saat kamu memutuskan tepat saat berbicara: sesuatu terjadi dan kamu memilih apa yang mau kamu lakukan. Kalau rencananya sudah ada dari sebelumnya (kamu sudah punya tiketnya), pakai going to. Kata 'akan' dalam bahasa Indonesia mencakup keduanya, jadi lihat situasinya, bukan kata Indonesianya.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with will and the verb in brackets: I think the meeting ___ (be) long today.
Make it negative: The shop will be open on Sunday.
expected: the shop won't be open on sunday
the shop will not be open on sunday
guidedPractice.hint: will not = won't. Don't change the other words.

guidedPractice.prompt: Your friend says: 'I don't understand this email in English.' Offer help with I'll.
Your boss says: 'It's so hot in here!' Answer with I'll + turn on + the fan.
expected: i will turn on the fan
guidedPractice.hint: You decide right now, so use I'll.

guidedPractice.prompt: Plan from before or decision now? Complete: 'My racket and shoes are in my bag. I ___ (play) badminton after work.'
guidedPractice.hint: The racket is already in the bag: the plan is from before.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one prediction about next weekend. Use I think … will.
expected: i think it will rain on saturday
i think i will be busy
i think we will go to the beach
independentPractice.hint: I think + subject + will + base form.

independentPractice.prompt: You're at a warung. You look at the menu and choose the mie goreng. Order it with I'll.
expected: i'll have the mie goreng please
i will have the mie goreng please

independentPractice.prompt: Your mum says: 'Call me when you get to Jakarta!' Make a promise.

assessment.prompt: Complete with will and the verb in brackets: Don't worry about the test tomorrow. I'm sure you ___ (pass).
assessment.rubric: Correct: will pass / 'll pass. 'will passes' or 'will passing' = 40. 'will to pass' = 40. 'pass' alone = 20. 'are going to pass' = 70 (a correct future, but the task asks for will).

assessment.prompt: Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: I think Pak Hasan will is angry.
acceptableAnswers: i think pak hasan will be angry
i think pak hasan'll be angry
assessment.rubric: Correct: I think Pak Hasan will be angry (after will, is → be). 'will angry' = 40. 'is angry' (no will) = 30. Repeating 'will is' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Translate into English with I'll (an offer): Saya bawakan tasmu.
acceptableAnswers: i'll carry your bag for you
i will carry your bag for you
assessment.rubric: Needs I'll / I will + carry (or take) + your bag. 'I carry your bag' = 30 (no will). 'I will to carry' = 40. 'I'm going to carry your bag' = 50. 'the bag' instead of 'your bag' = 90.

assessment.prompt: Your friend says: 'This is a secret!' Make a promise. Complete: Don't worry, I ___ tell anyone.
assessment.rubric: Correct: won't / will not. 'don't' = 30 (not a promise about the future). 'not will' or 'willn't' = 30. 'will' = 0 (opposite meaning).

assessment.prompt: The doorbell is ringing. Your friend is in the bathroom. Complete with the verb open: Stay there, I ___ the door.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 'll open / will open (a decision at this moment). 'open' alone = 30. 'am going to open' = 50 (going to is for a plan from before). 'am opening' = 40. 'will to open' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Complete with will or going to and the verb paint. Budi: 'Why do you have all this paint?' You: 'I ___ my bedroom this weekend.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: am / 'm going to paint (you already have the paint, so the plan is from before). Also accept 'am painting'. 'will paint' = 30. 'going to paint' without am = 60. 'paint' alone = 20.

blocks.text:
**will** talks about the future. After will, use the **base form** of the verb: the verb as you find it in the dictionary, with **no to**, **no -ing** and **no -s**.
- *I will call*, *she will call*, *they will call*: the same for every **subject** (the subject = who does it: *I, Rina, my parents*).
- **am / is / are** become **be**: *It will be hot*, not 'It will is hot'.

When people speak, **will** usually becomes **'ll**: *I'll, you'll, he'll, she'll, it'll, we'll, they'll*. The negative is **will not**, short form **won't**.

id.text:
**will** dipakai untuk membicarakan masa depan. Setelah will, pakai **bentuk dasar** kata kerja: kata kerja seperti di kamus, **tanpa to**, **tanpa -ing** dan **tanpa -s**.
- *I will call*, *she will call*, *they will call*: sama untuk semua **subjek** (subjek = siapa yang melakukan: *I, Rina, my parents*).
- **am / is / are** berubah menjadi **be**: *It will be hot*, bukan 'It will is hot'.

Saat berbicara, **will** biasanya disingkat menjadi **'ll**: *I'll, you'll, he'll, she'll, it'll, we'll, they'll*. Bentuk negatifnya **will not**, bentuk pendeknya **won't**.

id.note: bukan 'will comes': tidak ada -s setelah will

rows.note: not 'will to call': no to after will

id.note: bukan 'will to call': tidak ada to setelah will

rows.en: It will be sunny on Sunday.
We won't be at home tonight.
rows.id: Nanti malam kami tidak ada di rumah.

blocks.text: **won't** is an exception: the short form of *will not* is **won't**, not 'willn't'. Just remember it. Say it like **don't** with a *w* ('wount'). Don't say it like **want** ('wont', *mau*): *I won't go* (saya tidak akan pergi) and *I want to go* (saya mau pergi) mean very different things!

id.text: **won't** adalah pengecualian: bentuk pendek *will not* adalah **won't**, bukan 'willn't'. Hafalkan saja. Ucapkan seperti **don't** dengan *w* di depan ('wount'). Jangan diucapkan seperti **want** ('wont', *mau*): *I won't go* (saya tidak akan pergi) dan *I want to go* (saya mau pergi) artinya sangat berbeda!

blocks.explain: After will, am/is/are become **be**: *My sister will be 30 next year.* 'will is' has two verbs together, and 'will' alone has no verb.

id.explain: Setelah will, am/is/are berubah menjadi **be**: *My sister will be 30 next year.* 'will is' memakai dua kata kerja sekaligus, dan 'will' saja tidak punya kata kerja.

material.title: Predictions: what you think will happen

blocks.text:
A **prediction** is a guess about the future: what you think will happen. Use **will** with these starters:
- **I think** … *I think it will rain this afternoon.*
- **Maybe** … (at the start) *Maybe the bus will be late.*
- **I'm sure** … *I'm sure you'll like Bandung.*
- **I don't think** … *I don't think Budi will come.*

Why *I don't think Budi will come* and not *I think Budi won't come*? Both are correct, but English usually puts the *not* on *think*. In Indonesian we say *Saya rasa Budi tidak akan datang*, so this order feels strange at first.

id.text:
**Prediksi** adalah tebakan tentang masa depan: apa yang menurutmu akan terjadi. Pakai **will** dengan pembuka berikut:
- **I think** … (saya rasa) *I think it will rain this afternoon.*
- **Maybe** … (mungkin; di awal kalimat) *Maybe the bus will be late.*
- **I'm sure** … (saya yakin) *I'm sure you'll like Bandung.*
- **I don't think** … *I don't think Budi will come.*

Kenapa *I don't think Budi will come* dan bukan *I think Budi won't come*? Keduanya benar, tapi bahasa Inggris biasanya menaruh *not* pada *think*. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *Saya rasa Budi tidak akan datang*, jadi urutan ini awalnya terasa aneh.

rows.en: I think the traffic will be bad tonight.
I'm sure your parents will be happy.
rows.id: Saya yakin orang tuamu akan senang.

rows.en: I don't think it will be cold in Surabaya.
rows.id: Saya rasa di Surabaya tidak akan dingin.

blocks.text: Remember **going to** from the last lesson? When you **see the proof now** (dark clouds, a very full bus), **going to** is best: *Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.* When it's just **your opinion**, use **I think … will**. For opinions, both are often fine, so don't worry too much here.

id.text: Masih ingat **going to** dari pelajaran sebelumnya? Kalau kamu **melihat buktinya sekarang** (awan gelap, bus yang penuh sekali), **going to** paling tepat: *Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.* Kalau itu hanya **pendapatmu**, pakai **I think … will**. Untuk pendapat, keduanya sering sama-sama benar, jadi jangan terlalu khawatir di sini.

blocks.prompt: Don't take the bus at 5 p.m. I think the roads ___ very busy.
blocks.explain: will + base form: **will be**. No -ing after will ('will being'), and 'will very busy' has no verb: *busy* needs *be*.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Don't take the bus at 5 p.m. I think the roads ___ very busy.
id.explain: will + bentuk dasar: **will be**. Tidak ada -ing setelah will ('will being'), dan 'will very busy' tidak punya kata kerja: *busy* butuh *be*.

id.title: Prediksi: apa yang menurutmu akan terjadi

blocks.text:
**Offer** (menawarkan bantuan): you see a problem and say what you'll do: **I'll** + verb.
**Promise** (janji): you give your word: **I'll** … or **I won't** …. Add **I promise** to make it stronger.

The Indonesian trap: we often use no future word here. *Nanti saya telepon* or *Biar saya yang bayar* have no *akan*, so learners say 'I call you later' or 'I pay'. In English an offer or a promise needs **will**: **I'll call you later. I'll pay.**

id.text:
**Offer** (menawarkan bantuan): kamu melihat ada masalah dan bilang apa yang akan kamu lakukan: **I'll** + kata kerja.
**Promise** (janji): kamu memberi janji: **I'll** … atau **I won't** …. Tambahkan **I promise** supaya lebih kuat.

Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: di sini kita sering tidak memakai kata masa depan. *Nanti saya telepon* atau *Biar saya yang bayar* tidak memakai *akan*, jadi pelajar bilang 'I call you later' atau 'I pay'. Dalam bahasa Inggris, tawaran atau janji butuh **will**: **I'll call you later. I'll pay.**

rows.en: Put your wallet away. I'll pay.
rows.id: Simpan dompetmu. Biar saya yang bayar.

rows.en: I'll send you the photos tonight.

blocks.prompt: Your mum: 'Call me tonight!' You: 'OK, I ___ you.'
blocks.explain: This is a promise about tonight, so you need **will**: *OK, I'll call you.* 'I call you' is the Indonesian *saya telepon* word by word, with no future.

id.prompt: Ibumu: 'Call me tonight!' Kamu: 'OK, I ___ you.'
id.explain: Ini janji untuk nanti malam, jadi kamu butuh **will**: *OK, I'll call you.* 'I call you' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *saya telepon*, tanpa masa depan.

material.title: Decide now (will) or plan from before (going to)?

blocks.text:
Indonesian **akan** covers both **will** and **going to**, so the Indonesian word can't tell you which one to use. Look at the situation:
- You decide **at this moment**, because something happens now → **will**. *The phone's ringing. I'll answer it.*
- The plan is **from before**: you already have the tickets, the paint, the bag → **going to**. *I have the tickets. We're going to watch the film on Saturday.*

And careful: for a quick decision, Indonesian often has no future word at all (*Saya angkat*, *Saya ambil yang putih*). English still needs **'ll**: 'The phone's ringing. I answer it' is wrong.

id.text:
Kata **akan** dalam bahasa Indonesia mencakup **will** dan **going to**, jadi kata Indonesianya tidak bisa memberi tahu mana yang dipakai. Lihat situasinya:
- Kamu memutuskan **saat ini juga**, karena ada sesuatu yang terjadi sekarang → **will**. *The phone's ringing. I'll answer it.*
- Rencananya sudah ada **dari sebelumnya**: kamu sudah punya tiketnya, catnya, tasnya → **going to**. *I have the tickets. We're going to watch the film on Saturday.*

Hati-hati juga: untuk keputusan cepat, bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakai kata masa depan sama sekali (*Saya angkat*, *Saya ambil yang putih*). Bahasa Inggris tetap butuh **'ll**: 'The phone's ringing. I answer it' itu salah.

rows.en: There's no sugar. — OK, I'll buy some.
I'll have the soto ayam, please.
Here are the train tickets. We're going to visit Grandma on Sunday.
rows.id: Ini tiket keretanya. Hari Minggu kita akan mengunjungi Nenek.

rows.en: My suitcase is ready. I'm going to fly to Medan on Friday.
rows.id: Koperku sudah siap. Hari Jumat saya akan terbang ke Medan.

blocks.text: Quick test: could you say *Oh!* or *OK!* before it? *Oh, OK, I'll buy some.* That's a new decision → **will**. Could you say *I already have the plan*? → **going to**.

id.text: Tes cepat: bisakah kamu bilang *Oh!* atau *OK!* di depannya? *Oh, OK, I'll buy some.* Itu keputusan baru → **will**. Bisakah kamu bilang *rencananya sudah ada*? → **going to**.

blocks.prompt: Your colleague: 'The printer isn't working!' You: 'No problem. I ___ Pak Hasan. He can fix it.'
blocks.explain: You hear about the problem now and decide now, so use **will**: *I'll call Pak Hasan.* 'going to' is for a plan from before, and 'I call' has no future.

id.prompt: Rekan kerjamu: 'The printer isn't working!' Kamu: 'No problem. I ___ Pak Hasan. He can fix it.'
id.explain: Kamu baru tahu masalahnya sekarang dan memutuskan sekarang juga, jadi pakai **will**: *I'll call Pak Hasan.* 'going to' untuk rencana dari sebelumnya, dan 'I call' tidak menunjukkan masa depan.

id.title: Memutuskan sekarang (will) atau rencana dari sebelumnya (going to)?

id.intro: Hari ini kamu belajar **will**, kata kecil dengan banyak tugas. Kamu memakainya untuk mengatakan apa yang menurutmu akan terjadi (I think it will rain), untuk menawarkan bantuan dan berjanji (I'll help you), dan untuk memutuskan sesuatu saat itu juga (There's no milk? I'll buy some). Pemanasan: apa bahasa Inggrisnya 'Saya janji'?
